chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of A'yan, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
If he becomes certain that he added to the prescribed salat (prayer), he does not count it, and he begins his salat (prayer) anew, when he has become certain with certainty.

key_terms.زَادَ: added something extra beyond what is prescribed
key_terms.لَمْ يَعْتَدَّ بِهَا: he does not regard it as valid or count it

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he is certain that he added something to the obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding one who becomes certain that he has made an addition in the obligatory salat (prayer). In such a case, the prayer is not counted and must be restarted, with the ruling hinging upon definite certainty.
